_meta.name: abbott-components
_meta.title: GROW / Abbott component build hub
_meta.generatedBy: build-manifest.mjs (do not hand-edit components.manifest.json; edit this overlay or the source files, then regenerate)
_meta.purpose: Registry + fill-in template for the Adapt units matured in this workbench. To author a course block, copy a unit's content.block, fill the slots, and paste it into the build. To build or test the plugin itself, follow its agents.agent-author.shell pointers. Identity, file pointers and content are DERIVED from each unit's own files; this overlay supplies only the editorial parts (agents, maturity, install).
howToUse: 2. Read its `agents.agent-author` block for the right context (shell = build/test the plugin; content-pack = author a filled block).
3. For authoring: deep-copy `content.block`, replace every slot (see `_meta.conventions.slots`), validate each field against `content.fields`, paste into the target's `components.json`.
4. For building: run the unit's `files.test` command, then follow `install` to copy it into the Adapt build and `npx grunt build`.

slots.\"\": Empty string = a prose slot to fill (title, body, passage, heading...).
slots.<<...>>: Angle-bracket token = replace with the value the text describes (ids, parent ids, tagged text).
slots.array with one item: A skeleton item; duplicate it for as many entries as you need, or empty the array where the field is optional.
slots._ prefix: Keys beginning with `_` are Adapt config, not prose. Keep the provided defaults unless `content.fields` says otherwise; only `enum` values are legal.
slots.optional fields: `content.block` carries the common fields; `content.fields` documents every field, including optional ones (e.g. a scene's `_extras`) you can add by hand.
slots.seeded defaults: A unit's `seedFromExample` (in the overlay) lists block keys whose value is copied from the worked `example.json` instead of the bare schema default, giving richer starting text. List only config/instruction-type keys, not prose or content arrays.
slots.unchanged keys: `_type`, `_component`/`_extension` and `_layout` are fixed for the unit. Do not edit them.

kinds.library: Framework-agnostic engine. Not placed in a course and not authored directly; vendored into the plugins that use it.
kinds.component: An Adapt component placed on the page as a block in a `components.json`.
kinds.extension: An Adapt extension; switches on globally and reaches into existing content rather than being placed. Authored by tagging content and/or per-component attributes.

shell.who: An agent working in a terminal inside this repo (build hub is grow-course/wkspc2614-adapt3).
shell.goal: Mature, test, vendor-sync and install the plugin/library itself.
ground-rules: Run logic tests with `node --test <file>` from the unit folder; ESM test dirs carry a `package.json` with {"type":"module"} (keep it).
LESS compiles under the build's Less 3.x: write `:is(a, b)` as a plain comma selector list, and escape a literal `min()` as `~"min(...)"` so Less does not treat it as its own function.

Adapt plugins are self-contained and cannot import across plugin folders, so the grow-marks core is VENDORED into each plugin's `js/libs/` + `less/grow-marks.less`. Re-sync with the unit's `vendorResync` commands after changing the library.
Do not hand-edit vendored `js/libs/*` or `less/grow-marks.less` in a plugin; edit `grow-marks` and re-sync.
The wider course build has its own gotchas (python3 shim, uppercase L## lesson keys, 3-outcome model) — see grow-course-authoring-recipe; they are not needed to build these units in isolation.

content-pack.who: An agent (or author) filling a unit with course content, in a content pack / lesson-authoring pass.
content-pack.goal: Produce a valid, filled block (or tagged text) ready to drop into a course's `components.json` / `course.json`.
ground-rules: House style: no em dashes. Use commas, parentheses or a full stop.
Fill every `""` and `<<...>>` slot; leave optional `_`-config at its default unless you mean to change it.
Only values listed in a field's `enum` are legal; unknown values silently fall back to the default, they do not error.
Keep `_id` unique within the course and set `_parentId` to the real id of the block the component sits in.
Prose is learner-facing: keep headings short, bodies tight; mind any per-field length note in `content.fields`.

Every prose slot (fields tagged `voice: prose`, plus title/displayTitle/body) must satisfy `_meta.voice`: British spelling, no em dash, no banned phrase, no 'There is/are' opener, sentences under the word limit. Write to it as you generate, do not fix it afterwards.
content-pack.verify: Draft the block into a temp .json, then run `_meta.voice.run` against it; fix any violation before paste. The lint is a hard gate.

maturity.notes: Artwork ported from the marks.html / bullets.html studies. Not an Adapt plugin.

content.note: Not placed in a course and not filled with content directly. Its marks reach learners through the adapt-grow-marks extension (data-gm-* spans + question feedback) and the adapt-grow-annotate component. Author there, not here.

shell.goal: Maintain the engine: extend the catalogue, keep the pure logic correct, keep it runnable unbundled.
steps: Edit artwork/data in src/marksCatalogue.js, pure helpers in src/marksLogic.js, DOM engine in src/growMarks.js.
Use explicit `.js` extensions on relative imports so it runs in the browser, in Node and through Rollup.
Run the tests; preview visually via the demo.
After any change, re-vendor into every plugin that uses it (see those units' vendorResync).

commands.demo: npx serve abbott/components/grow-marks   # then open /demo/ (module imports need http, not file://)

maturity.notes: Interaction, marks, labels, completion and reset all work. Known v1 follow-up: persisting the annotations themselves into LMS suspend data across a full reload.

then: add the component block to a block's components.json (see example.json)

shell.goal: Build/test the component and keep its vendored engine in sync.
steps: Pure logic lives in js/annotateLogic.js (parse passage, apply/toggle state, completion, (de)serialise). Keep view imperative: it renders the JSX shell once then wires targets by hand, so appended mark SVGs are never discarded.
Run the logic tests.
If grow-marks changed, re-vendor before building.
Install into the build and run grunt.

content-pack.goal: Author one annotate block: pick annotatable words and a small tool palette.
steps: Write the passage; wrap 3-8 selectable words in [[brackets]]. Give a reused word a stable key: [[word|key]].
Define 1-3 tools (id + label + mark + colour). One tool => circle-the-word toggle.
Set _minAnnotations to what counts as 'engaged' (often 2).
Set a unique _id and the real _parentId.
rules: Only marks/colours from the enums in content.fields are legal.
Keep the passage readable as plain text with the brackets stripped.

maturity.notes: Scope is deliberate: it marks author-tagged targets and reacts to question state; it does not pick arbitrary words at runtime.

then: npm run adapt-install  # register the extension

content.unit: extension attribute (no block of its own)
content.note: An extension is not placed on the page. You author it in two ways:

tagWords.where: Inside any text field (body, instruction, item text...) in any component.
tagWords.template: A word to mark.

data-gm-mark.help: Any catalogue id: oval, underline, box, highlight, tick, star, cross, ...

data-gm-hold.help: Keep the mark after it draws (default true).

questionFeedback.where: On a question component (mcq, etc.). Opt-in so it never fights the question's own feedback.

_isEnabled.help: Turn on to play a mark when this question is answered.

_target.help: CSS selector inside the component to place the mark on. Defaults to a [data-gm-feedback] element, then the title.

disable.where: course.json (whole course) or on a single component.

shell.goal: Build/test the extension and keep its vendored engine in sync.
steps: Pure enablement + mark resolution in js/marksExtensionLogic.js; the extension body (js/adapt-grow-marks.js) plays tagged spans via IntersectionObserver on pageView:ready and feedback on questionView:showFeedback.
Run the logic tests.
Re-vendor grow-marks if it changed.
Install into the build (extensions path), run adapt-install, then grunt.

content-pack.goal: Add marks to existing content: tag words and/or turn on question feedback.
steps: To make words draw on: wrap them in <span data-gm-mark="..." data-gm-color="..."> in the component's text (see patterns.tagWords).
To mark a question right/wrong: add the _growMarks._feedback object to that question (see patterns.questionFeedback).
Tag sparingly, a few marks per screen; the effect is emphasis, not decoration everywhere.
rules: Tag the specific word or target a selector; the extension will not pick words for you.
Marks are decorative (aria-hidden); never rely on a mark to carry meaning a screen reader needs.
Only enum values are legal; no em dashes in prose.

maturity.notes: Matured from the scroll-scenes study. The old scenes.py / YAML pipeline is retired; content + look now map onto authoring fields.

then: add the component block to a block's components.json (see example.json)

shell.goal: Build/test the component; mind the Less 3.x idioms.
steps: Pure maths + the preset/override resolver live in js/scrollScenesLogic.js; the driver writes --scene-offset / --scene-distance each frame so transition models work with no external bridge.
Run the logic tests.
LESS: keep `:is(...)` as comma lists and the escaped `~"min(...)"` (Less 3.x).
Install into the build and run grunt.

content-pack.goal: Author a scroll-scenes block: a short sequence of scenes plus one chosen look.
steps: Pick a _preset for the whole block; leave the override dials blank unless you mean to change one.

Write 3-5 scenes. Each: a short stageLabel, a heading (use
, ~20 chars/line), a tight body.
Add _extras only where a scene earns a prompt; leave transitionCue blank on the last scene.
Set a unique _id and the real _parentId.
rules: Only enum values are legal; an unknown value falls back to the preset, it does not error.
Design is authored, not shown: there is no learner-facing settings toolbar, so choose the look here.
